cards.front: Name the 8 energy stores.
cards.back: Kinetic, Gravitational Potential, Elastic Potential, Chemical, Thermal, Nuclear, Magnetic, Electrostatic.

cards.front: What is the unit of energy?
cards.back: Joule (J)

cards.front: Formula for kinetic energy:
cards.back: Ek = ½ mv² (mass in kg, velocity in m/s, energy in J)

cards.front: Formula for gravitational potential energy:
cards.back: Ep = mgh (mass in kg, g = 9.8 N/kg, height in m, energy in J)

cards.front: Formula for elastic potential energy:
cards.back: Ee = ½ ke² (spring constant k in N/m, extension e in m, energy in J)

cards.front: A 2kg ball is thrown at 5 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
A 60kg student climbs 10m. Calculate GPE gained. (g = 10 N/kg)
What is the law of conservation of energy?
cards.back: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores. Total energy in a closed system remains constant.

cards.front: What happens to energy when work is done against friction?
cards.back: Transferred to thermal energy store (heat).

cards.front: Formula for work done:
cards.back: W = F × s (Force in N, distance in m in direction of force, Work in J)

cards.front: A force of 50N moves an object 4m. Work done?
What is power? Unit?
cards.back: Rate of energy transfer. Unit: Watt (W) = 1 J/s

cards.front: Formula for power:
cards.back: P = E ÷ t (Energy in J, time in s, Power in W)

cards.front: A motor does 5000J of work in 10s. Power?
What is specific heat capacity? Unit?
cards.back: Energy needed to raise 1kg of a substance by 1°C. Unit: J/kg°C

cards.front: Formula for energy change with temperature:
cards.back: ΔE = mcΔθ (mass in kg, specific heat capacity c in J/kg°C, temp change Δθ in °C)

cards.front: How can you reduce unwanted energy transfers?
cards.back: Lubrication (reduce friction), insulation (reduce thermal transfer), streamlining (reduce air resistance).

cards.front: Formula for efficiency:
cards.back: Efficiency = Useful output energy ÷ Total input energy × 100%

cards.front: A kettle uses 200,000J to heat water. 180,000J heats the water. Efficiency?
What are the main energy resources? Classify as renewable/non-renewable.
cards.back: Renewable: Solar, Wind, Hydro, Tidal, Geothermal, Biomass. Non-renewable: Coal, Oil, Gas, Nuclear.
